title: Byron Buxton trying to return to Twins despite needing hip surgery
content:
CHICAGO — The Minnesota Twins are working with Byron Buxton on a potential return before the season ends, but also are preparing for him to undergo offseason hip surgery.

On the 10-day injured list retroactive to Aug. 27, Buxton has been rendered ineffective for more than two months while battling a right hip impingement. Though he’s dealt with the issue multiple times since the 2021 season, the three-time All-Star’s hip has bothered him enough this season to result in three trips to the IL.

Despite receiving an injection in July to improve his condition, Buxton has played only 18 games in the second half with a .477 OPS.

“Surgery is part of it,” Twins manager Derek Shelton said. “We’ll see where he’s at over the next week, the next few days, wherever he’s at and see how it improves. And then when we have to make the determination on where he’s at.”

At this point, what type of surgery Buxton will require is to be determined. Currently, Buxton is restricted from baseball activities and is strictly focused on recovery, trying to return at some point over the team’s final 22 games.

Buxton must be hoping for a repeat of the 2024 season when he returned to action for the final two weeks after a 28-game layoff due to a sore hip. He produced an .840 OPS in 53 plate appearances during those final 12 games.

He’s been on the IL since injuring himself on Aug. 25 in West Sacramento, Calif., on a play in the outfield when Buxton was unable to reach down and grab a ball he was pursuing.

“We’ve got to get this in a little bit better spot for me to be able to do what I was doing,” Buxton said on Aug. 26. “I figured we would have to manage it throughout the season. When we get to the end of the season, figure out where to go from that point forward.”

Now, the Twins are weighing what the best course of action is for Buxton. Even though they know he’ll need surgery and then time to rehab, the Twins are giving him a chance to return before the season ends.

“The difficulty is because you’ve got to work your way back into baseball activity,” Shelton said. “We only have 22 games left. … The biggest component to this is the teammate that Buck is and his want to get back. We owe it to him to be able to explore all those options before we go down a different route.”
